question_text: What do the terms phycobiont and mycobiont signify?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The two terms
lines: In a lichen, the algal partner is the phycobiont.
The fungal partner is the mycobiont.
steps.why: A lichen is a symbiotic association of an alga and a fungus, and these two terms name the two partners.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two terms. Phyco- means alga; myco- means fungus.
Writing lichen as a single organism with no partners.
steps.memory_tip: Phyco- as in phycology (study of algae); myco- as in mycology (study of fungi).
steps.margin_note: Name both partners; one term alone is half the point.

steps.label: Role of each partner
lines: The phycobiont is autotrophic: it prepares
The mycobiont is heterotrophic: it provides
shelter and absorbs water and mineral

lines.text: Phycobiont = alga; mycobiont = fungus of a lichen.

steps.why: The two partners survive together because each supplies what the other cannot make: food from the alga; shelter, water and minerals from the fungus.
common_mistakes: Stopping after naming the partners. The word signify asks what each one does.
Writing that the fungus makes food. Only the algal partner photosynthesises.
steps.memory_tip: Alga feeds; fungus houses. One role line for each.
steps.margin_note: One role line for each partner completes the answer.

insider_note: The word signify asks for the role of each partner, not only the naming — the second mark sits in the role lines.
